title: The Cell Cycle
seo_title: Biology 1: The Cell Cycle Worksheets (Strengthened SHS)
standard_text: The cell cycle (interphase and the mitotic phase); mitosis and cytokinesis; meiosis and its importance; disorders from errors in cell division such as cancer. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Biology 1, Quarter 1)
meta_desc: Free Biology 1 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 1): the cell cycle, mitosis, meiosis, meiosis and variation and cancer, stem cells and specialization. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mitosis copies cells; meiosis makes sex cells.
key_sub: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents.
body_html:
How to think about it

In mitosis one cell divides into two identical cells with the same number of chromosomes. It is used for growth and repair, and for asexual reproduction, where one parent makes offspring that are genetically identical (binary fission, budding, runners, cuttings).

Meiosis makes sex cells (gametes) with half the number of chromosomes: 23 in humans. In sexual reproduction two gametes join at fertilization, so the offspring get a mix of genes from two parents. This variation helps a population survive change.

Example

A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many does a sperm cell have?

Meiosis halves the number.

Answer: 23

Example

A strawberry plant grows new plants from runners. What kind of reproduction is this?

Only one parent

Answer: asexual

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mitosis and meiosis.
  • Thinking asexual offspring are different from the parent.
  • Thinking sexual reproduction is faster.

faq.q: What is an advantage of asexual reproduction?
faq.a: It is fast and needs only one parent.
If the environment changes, some individuals may have traits that help them survive.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate)?
items.e: Metaphase: chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate).

items.q: Which stage is this? The cell looks pinched in the middle as it splits in two.
items.e: Cytokinesis: The cell looks pinched in the middle as it splits in two.

items.q: What happens in G₁ phase?
c: the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles
the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells
items.e: G₁ phase: the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate.

items.q: Which stage comes right after prophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What happens in G₂ phase?
c: DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
items.e: G₂ phase: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing.

items.q: Which stage is this? The cytoplasm splits and two daughter cells form.
items.e: Cytokinesis: The cytoplasm splits and two daughter cells form.

items.q: Which stage is this? Spindle fibers attach to the centromeres at the cell's middle line.
items.e: Metaphase: Spindle fibers attach to the centromeres at the cell's middle line.

items.q: What happens in prophase?
c: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles
the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
items.e: Prophase: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form.

items.q: Which stage is this? Chromosomes condense and become visible; the nuclear membrane breaks down.
items.e: Prophase: Chromosomes condense and become visible; the nuclear membrane breaks down.

items.q: What happens in anaphase?
c: the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
items.e: Anaphase: the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes?
items.e: Telophase: nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes.

items.q: Which cells keep dividing throughout life in plants?
items.e: e.g. root and shoot tips.

items.q: Which stage comes right before cytokinesis?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage is this? Two new nuclei form around the chromosomes at each end.
items.e: Telophase: Two new nuclei form around the chromosomes at each end.

items.q: Which stage comes right after metaphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What is the longest phase of meiosis I prophase in oocytes of some vertebrates?
c: diplotene, which can last months or years
items.e: Oocytes stay in diplotene for a long time.

items.q: What happens to the DNA content in the S phase?
items.e: The chromosome number stays 2n.

items.q: Which stage comes right before anaphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What is the significance of mitosis?
c: creating genetic variation by crossing over
growth, repair and keeping the chromosome number the same
items.e: It replaces worn-out cells.

items.q: How does cytokinesis happen in plant cells?
c: a furrow forms from the outside
a cell plate forms in the middle and grows outward
items.e: Animal cells form a cleavage furrow.

items.q: A mouse cell has 40 chromosomes. After DNA replication, how many sister chromatids are there?
items.e: Each chromosome is copied: 40 × 2 = 80.

items.q: A human cell with 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in both daughter cells together?
items.e: Two cells × 46 = 92.

items.q: A mouse cell with 40 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in both daughter cells together?
items.e: Two cells × 40 = 80.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 15 of 400 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 3.75%.

items.q: A fruit fly body cell has 8 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell after mitosis?
items.e: Mitosis makes identical cells with the same number.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 18 hours. In a sample, 30 of 250 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 30/250 × 1,080 min = 130 min.

items.e: Mitosis makes identical cells with the same number.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 20 hours. In a sample, 18 of 240 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 18/240 × 1,200 min = 90.0 min.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 12 hours. In a sample, 18 of 400 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 18/400 × 720 min = 32.4 min.

items.e: Two cells × 48 = 96.

items.q: Mitosis: are the new cells identical?
items.e: Meiosis: no, genetically different. Mitosis: yes, identical.

items.q: Meiosis: main purpose?
items.e: Meiosis: making gametes for sexual reproduction. Mitosis: growth and repair.

items.q: Mitosis: chromosome number in new cells?
items.e: Meiosis: half (haploid). Mitosis: same (diploid).

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous pairs line up in the middle of the cell.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: Meiosis: number of cells produced?
items.e: Meiosis: four. Mitosis: two.

items.q: Meiosis: number of divisions?
items.e: Meiosis: two. Mitosis: one.

items.q: Meiosis: are the new cells identical?
items.e: Meiosis: no, genetically different. Mitosis: yes, identical.

items.q: What happens in zygotene of meiosis?
c: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
chiasmata terminalize and the nuclear envelope breaks down
crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
items.e: Zygotene: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents.

items.q: What happens in anaphase II of meiosis?
c: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits
homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen
items.e: Anaphase II: sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous chromosomes pair up and swap pieces (crossing over).
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Single chromosomes line up in the middle of two cells.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A dog egg and sperm each have 39 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
A fruit fly cell (2n = 8) finishes meiosis I. How many chromosomes are in each of the two new cells?
items.e: Homologs separate in meiosis I, so each cell has 4 (each still with two chromatids).

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Four haploid cells are formed.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
In which stage of meiosis does this happen: chiasmata terminalize and the nuclear envelope breaks down?
items.e: Diakinesis: chiasmata terminalize and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Sister chromatids separate to opposite poles.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A chicken body cell has 78 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
In which stage of meiosis does this happen: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules?
items.e: Pachytene: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules.

items.q: Mitosis: number of divisions?
items.e: Meiosis: two. Mitosis: one.

items.q: A species has 6 pairs of chromosomes. How many different chromosome combinations can occur in zygotes from random fertilization (ignoring crossing over)?
A diploid cell of a fungus has 46 chromosomes. How many different combinations of chromosomes can its gametes have by independent segregation?
items.e: With n = 23 pairs, combinations = 2n = 8,388,608.

items.q: A gamete of a fish has 4 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 8.

items.q: A species has 5 pairs of chromosomes. How many different chromosome combinations can occur in zygotes from random fertilization (ignoring crossing over)?
A gamete of an animal has 3 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 6.

items.q: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 23.

items.q: Which is a polygenic trait?
items.e: Many genes plus environment give continuous variation.

items.q: A gamete of a species of fruit fly has 23 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 46.

items.q: A rice egg and sperm each have 12 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
A diploid body cell of a plant has 10 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in one of its gametes?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: 5.

items.q: A diploid body cell of a fish has 16 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in one of its gametes?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: 8.

items.q: A diploid body cell of a plant has 24 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in one of its gametes?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: 12.

items.q: A gamete of a fish has 2 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 4.

items.q: What is the phenotype of an organism?
c: the DNA sequence of one gene
its observable characteristics, produced by genotype and environment
items.e: Genotype + environment → phenotype.

items.q: A corn body cell has 20 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 10.

items.q: A gamete of a species of fruit fly has 5 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 10.

items.q: A chimpanzee body cell has 48 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 24.

items.q: What is an allele?
c: a different form of the same gene
a section of a chromosome with many genes
items.e: For example, alleles for blood group A, B and O.

items.q: A diploid body cell of a plant has 12 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in one of its gametes?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: 6.

items.q: A gamete of a fish has 8 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 16.

items.q: What is a unipotent stem cell?
c: one that can become any cell
one that can only become one type of cell
items.e: For example cardiomyocytes from heart stem cells.

items.q: Which statement about meristem tissue in plants is true?
c: They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become almost any type of cell.
They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
items.e: It is found at the tips of roots and shoots.

items.q: mRNA: UUUUGGCUU. Codons: CUU = Leu, UGG = Trp, UUU = Phe, CGU = Arg, GCA = Ala. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UUU UGG CUU.

items.q: mRNA: AUGUUCGAU. Codons: AUG = Met, GAU = Asp, UUC = Phe, AUU = Ile. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: AUG UUC GAU.

items.q: How might high estrogen levels increase the risk of breast cancer?
c: estrogen can switch on genes that promote cell division
items.e: Fat tissue after the menopause makes estrogen.

items.q: Which statement about adult stem cells from bone marrow is true?
c: They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become almost any type of cell.
They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
items.e: They are taken from the patient or a donor.

items.q: What is cloning rare plants quickly and cheaply from meristems?
c: a use of plant stem cells
a possible future use of stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: What is treating paralysis by replacing damaged nerve cells?
c: a use of plant stem cells
a possible future use of stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: Cells lining the intestine are replaced every few days. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.

items.q: Which type of stem cell can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells?
c: adult stem cells from bone marrow
items.e: They are taken from the patient or a donor.

items.q: What is RNA interference (RNAi)?
c: small RNA molecules bind to mRNA and stop it being translated
items.e: siRNA and miRNA are involved.

items.q: A stem cell in the brain becomes a neuron. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.

items.q: A skin cut heals as new skin cells are made. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.

items.q: What is growing crops with special features, such as disease resistance?
c: a possible future use of stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
a use of plant stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: Which type of stem cell can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life?
c: adult stem cells from bone marrow
items.e: It is found at the tips of roots and shoots.

items.q: An embryo's cells become heart, nerve and skin cells. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.

items.q: What is a bone marrow transplant for leukemia?
c: a possible future use of stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
a use of plant stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: What does siRNA do?
c: guides an enzyme to cut a complementary mRNA
items.e: The mRNA cannot then be translated.

items.q: What is treating diabetes by making insulin-producing cells?
c: a use of plant stem cells
a possible future use of stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: Which statement about embryonic stem cells is true?
c: They can become almost any type of cell.
They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
items.e: There are ethical objections because embryos are destroyed.
